source.title: The magical number 4 in short-term memory: a reconsideration of mental storage capacity

confidence_rationale: The L3 capacity anchor: Cowan's wide-ranging synthesis argues the pure capacity limit of the focus of attention is a small fixed number averaging about 4 chunks (3-5), distinct from Miller's compound 7. This grounds two things the deliberation roadmap needs: (1) a principled prior on SD-046's slot count N (2-4, not arbitrary), and (2) the capacity-limited-selection premise behind SD-027/MECH-254's top-k gate. Held to 0.62: the transfer from human STM chunks to goal slots / selected latents is an analogy across domains, and Cowan's 'focus of attention' is not goals specifically; it bounds the count without being measured on goal maintenance.
failure_signatures: Cowan's limit is for the focus of attention over chunks; if 'goal slot' or 'selected E1/E2 latent' is not the right unit of chunking, the ~4 number may not transfer -- the capacity bound could be on something REE does not represent as a slot.

The capacity is a CENTRAL focus-of-attention limit, with non-capacity-limited stores (activated LTM) alongside it; an REE design that treats all maintained goals as occupying the capacity-limited focus would over-constrain, when biology allows many activated-but-not-focal goals plus a small focal set.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A single central capacity limit -- the focus of attention -- holds about 4 chunks (range 3-5) under conditions where chunking and rehearsal are controlled, smaller and more precise than Miller's 7. This pure capacity is distinct from non-capacity-limited stores (sensory memory, activated long-term memory).
mapping.ree_translation: SD-046's choice of N>=2 simultaneously-active goal slots (the roadmap says 'n=2-4 plausibly') is bounded from above by the focus-of-attention capacity: a small fixed number around 4. SD-027/MECH-254's capacity-limited top-k selection gate (k ~ 3-7 in the claim text) is the same bound applied to E1/E2 content entering E3. Cowan supplies the empirical prior that this number is small and fixed, not free -- and distinguishes the small FOCAL set from a larger activated-but-not-selected pool.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Cowan measures human short-term storage of chunks (digits, items), not goal slots or latent broadcast units; the ~4 number transfers as an order-of-magnitude prior on N and k, not as a measured value for goal maintenance. The focal/activated distinction warns against treating every maintained goal as occupying capacity.
mapping.source_context: Human short-term memory; cross-paradigm synthesis (BBS target article); healthy adults.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical, foundational BBS target article (source_quality 0.88). Mapping_fidelity 0.6: bounds the slot/selection count as a prior, but 'chunk' != 'goal slot' != 'selected latent'. Transfer_risk 0.42 -- the highest in this pull -- because the cross-domain transfer (human STM -> artificial goal slots) is a genuine analogy, not a measured isomorphism.
